title: Recognize extension-field tensors and construct special-linear transporters
body:
This enabling algebraic result recognizes arbitrary square tensors over an explicitly supplied finite field F_q that are isotopic to F_q[x_i]/(x_i^(p^h_i)). It returns the heights and all three factor maps, then removes the algebra-class promise from the existing determinant-character formula. It computes a complete special-linear orbit label and constructs determinant-one maps between equivalent accepted tensors. **The complete kappa calculation is unchanged.** A physical producer/consumer and its full paid bill remain open.

The [proof and scope](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/86389e525d3efafe236e929f6ae401c68be1d115/research/extension-field-tensor-recognition/README.md), [recognizer and transporters](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/86389e525d3efafe236e929f6ae401c68be1d115/research/extension-field-tensor-recognition/recognize.py), [exact verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/86389e525d3efafe236e929f6ae401c68be1d115/research/extension-field-tensor-recognition/verify.py) and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/86389e525d3efafe236e929f6ae401c68be1d115/research/extension-field-tensor-recognition/SOURCES.json) are pinned to this head. The base is `6cf7a683f447b9f1e2333791907fd92be5009a63`, priority revision 7; canonical main and live overlap were refreshed before submission without a guidance change.

The new field contract separates q-power radical recovery from semilinear p-power height kernels. Over F4, in the basis `(1,a+x)` of F4[x]/x^2 with a^2=a+1, the ordinary kernel of the squaring columns contains `(a^2,1)`, which represents `1+x` and squares to 1. The corrected kernel contains `(a,1)`, which represents x and squares to zero. Thus treating those columns as an ordinary linear map gives a wrong certificate. The composed algorithm has deterministic polynomial cost in tensor dimension for each fixed q. It does not claim polynomial bit complexity in log q or recognize every commutative algebra.

Verification covers all 65,536 F4 2x2x2 tensors against a separate complete GL2^3 orbit generator; exactly 13,500 pass. All 256 binary tensors also agree, with 54 accepted. Ninety changed-basis presentations over F2,F3,F4,F8,F9,F16,F25 check 2,322 basis products. Ninety determinant-one transporters check another 2,322 products. There are 125 failure controls, including reducible field moduli, nonregular modules, extra relations, wrong Frobenius kernels, changed transporters and unequal special-linear labels. Cutoff four and two cutoff-two variables over F4 have orbit counts three and one, and explicit maps attain all three labels in the first case.

Python 3.12 and its standard library suffice:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/extension-field-tensor-recognition
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/extension-field-tensor-recognition
```

The expected check markers are:

```text
PASS_EXTENSION_FIELD_TENSOR_RECOGNITION
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/extension-field-tensor-recognition outcome=completed
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES
```

Both registered checks, the nine-file committed-byte check, export validation and a Git-free optimized scientific replay passed. CI is pending at publication. The source-history preflight was not run in the shallow checkout. No predecessor full executable suite, proof-assistant build, independent human review, native supplier, physical precision/movement audit or selected cold replay was run. The finite orbit checks corroborate the written theorem; they do not establish a multiplication theorem.

Credit: Ali Romman's [PR #5540](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5540) supplies the regular-module reconstruction and released handoff; [PR #5525](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5525) supplies its earlier tensor implementation. Nick Petalas (@petalas) supplies the nucleus lineage through [PR #5252](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5252). apoursh (@apoursh) supplies the prime-field height criterion in [PR #5502](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5502), and Ali Romman's [PR #5459](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5459) supplies the finite-field character theorem. Their retained [reconstruction proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6cf7a683f447b9f1e2333791907fd92be5009a63/research/nonreduced-tensor-recognition/README.md), [height proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6cf7a683f447b9f1e2333791907fd92be5009a63/research/frobenius-algebra-recognition/PROOF.md) and [character proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6cf7a683f447b9f1e2333791907fd92be5009a63/research/frobenius-tensor-characters/README.md) are unchanged and authenticated. David Ganz and the linked atlas sources retain their credit. New proof, implementation and checks: Ali Romman (@aliromman), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
